_why: One table of hand-worked bets, run through BOTH graders: src/bet_log.py in
Python and the gradeBet/betCLV pair inside site/research/index.html in the
browser. Bets are now entered on the site and graded there, while the old
Google Sheet path is still parsed and matched in Python -- so the same book
is served by two implementations, and two implementations of anything
eventually disagree. This file is what stops that: tools/test_tracking.py
and tools/qa/research.mjs both read it, and either one going red on a case
the other passes is the disagreement showing up as a failed build instead of
as a percentage nobody can reconcile.
SIGN CONVENTIONS, because they are opposite on purpose:
game.line  is the market's number from the HOME side, positive when the
home team is favoured. Georgia -10 is line: 10.
case.line  is the number the BET took, from the BET's own side. Laying is
negative, taking is positive. Georgia -10 is line: -10.
units_won is rounded to 3dp, as both graders do. clv is null where no closing
price exists to compare against -- moneylines, here and in both graders.

g1._why: Home wins 31-24: by 7, total 55. Closing spread home -10, total 52.5.

tie._why: A drawn game. Cannot happen in college football, and the branch exists anyway.

unplayed._why: Not final. An ungraded bet must stay ungraded, never default to a loss.

cases.why: home laid 10 and won by 7 — the invisible one: flip the sign and it grades as a win
away took 10 and lost by 7 — the same bet from the other side
home -3 wins by 7
home -7 wins by exactly 7 — push, stake back
away +7 is the same push from the other side
half points cannot push, which is why books use them — -6.5 wins
…and -7.5 loses
stake scales the payout, not the result: 2.5u at -110
a 2.5u loss costs exactly 2.5u — losing is always the stake
price changes the payout: a +320 spread win pays 3.2u
laying more points than the close is negative CLV
taking more points than the close is positive CLV
a -400 favourite winning returns 0.25u — the hit rate alone would hide this
a +320 dog losing costs 1u
a moneyline has no closing number stored, so it has no CLV — null, not zero
over 52.5 with 55 on the board
under 52.5 with 55 on the board
over 55 with exactly 55 pushes
an over bought below the close is positive CLV
…and the under at the same number is negative CLV, and also loses
a drawn game pushes the moneyline rather than losing it
a pick'em on a drawn game pushes
laying into a draw still loses
an unfinished game is not a loss — it is not anything yet
